title: Inside the 6R80 Planetary Assembly
introduction:
A planetary gearset is a small mechanical solar system: planet gears sit around a central sun gear inside an outer ring gear. The clever part is choosing which member receives drive, which is held still and which carries rotation onward. I track those roles before trying to make sense of a ratio.

This overview covers the 6R80 automatic transmission. Use the cutaway to locate the assemblies inside the transmission, then the exploded view and shared parts key to separate their identities. The ratios below describe the stated gearset relationships; they are not automatically whole-transmission ratios. The drawings explain arrangement and power flow, rather than providing a teardown or assembly procedure.

edits.text: Planetary Gearsets in Cutaway
edits.why: The torque converter is at the left and the output end is at the right. I use this view to see how the highlighted front and rear gearsets fit around the transmission's central shaft.

edits.text: Planetary Gearsets in Exploded View
edits.why: The separated front group sits above and to the left of the rear group. Match each callout to the unchanged parts key, then return to the cutaway to see where that component lives.

edits.text: What the Mechanical Components Do
How the Planetary Gearsets Work
The transmission combines 2 planetary gearsets, front and rear, to provide reverse and 6 forward speeds.
edits.why: The gearsets work together; their individual relationships explain how the transmission builds its available ratios.

edits.text: The front assembly is a single planetary gearset made up of the following members:
edits.why: Identify its sun, carrier and ring before following the drive path.

edits.text: Front planetary No. 1 sun gear, the central gear.
Front planetary carrier, which carries the planet gears.
Front planetary ring gear, the outer gear forming part of the input shaft assembly.
edits.why: Its connection to the input shaft makes it the front gearset's driving member.

edits.text: The input shaft drives the front ring gear. The front sun gear is connected to the fluid pump and held stationary. With the sun held, the rotating ring drives the front planetary carrier assembly at a reduction ratio of 1.52:1.
edits.why: Holding the sun gives the planet gears a stationary member to work against, so the carrier turns at a reduced speed relative to the driving ring.

edits.text: In reverse, 1st gear, 2nd gear and 3rd gear, the front planetary carrier assembly is the front gearset's only output member. It supplies the rear planetary gearset through a 1.52:1 reduction.
edits.why: Here, the rear assembly receives its drive through the reduced-speed carrier path.

edits.text: In 4th gear and 5th gear, both the front ring gear and the front planetary carrier assembly act as outputs. They feed different rear planetary members through paths with ratios of 1:1 and 1.52:1.
edits.why: The rear gearset receives drive through both a direct-speed path and a reduced-speed path. It is more useful to follow those separate paths than to imagine a single output from the front assembly.

edits.text: In 6th gear, the front ring gear is the front gearset's only output member, supplying the rear planetary gearset at a 1:1 ratio.
edits.why: The drive path now uses the ring directly rather than taking output through the reduced-speed carrier.

edits.text: The rear assembly is a Ravigneaux planetary gearset containing the following members:
edits.why: Its sun gears and shared carrier provide several combinations of driven and held members.

edits.text: Rear planetary No. 2 sun gear.
Rear planetary No. 3 sun gear.
Rear planetary carrier assembly, carrying 2 sets of pinion gears.
edits.why: The carrier supports the pinion gears within the rear assembly.

edits.text: Rear planetary ring gear assembly, the outer member.
For each operating gear below, follow the driven member, any held member and the rear gearset's output:
edits.why: I read these as a cast list for each gear: who supplies motion, who stays put and who passes motion onward.

edits.text: In reverse, rear sun gear No. 2 is driven and the rear planetary carrier is held stationary. The ring gear provides the output at 2.24:1, with rotation reversed.
edits.why: The held carrier establishes the relationship that reverses the output direction.

edits.text: In 1st gear, sun gear No. 3 is driven and the rear planetary carrier is held stationary. The ring gear provides the output at 2.74:1.
edits.why: The carrier remains the held member, while the choice of driven sun establishes the forward reduction.

edits.text: In 2nd gear, sun gear No. 3 is driven and sun gear No. 2 is held stationary. The ring gear provides the output at 1.54:1.
edits.why: Changing which member is held changes the reduction even though the same sun receives drive.

edits.text: In 3rd gear, sun gear No. 3 and sun gear No. 2 are both driven. The ring gear provides the output at 1:1.
edits.why: This is the rear gearset's direct relationship; the front gearset's contribution still matters when considering the complete transmission.

edits.text: In 4th gear, sun gear No. 3 and the rear planetary carrier are driven. The ring gear provides the output at 1.14:1.
edits.why: This combination uses driven members supplied through the front assembly's separate output paths.

edits.text: In 5th gear, sun gear No. 2 and the rear planetary carrier are driven. The ring gear provides the output at 0.87:1.
edits.why: The driven sun changes while the carrier also receives drive, producing the stated overdrive relationship.

edits.text: In 6th gear, the rear planetary carrier is driven and sun gear No. 2 is held stationary. The ring gear provides the output at 0.69:1.
edits.why: The carrier supplies motion and the held sun establishes the rear assembly's overdrive relationship.
